paper_title: ATPlace2.5D: Analytical Thermal-Aware Chiplet Placement Framework for Large-Scale 2.5D-IC

scenario.description: Thermal-aware chiplet placement optimization for Case 3: 8 dies with 8448 nets on 39.0mm x 39.0mm interposer with 0.6 whitespace ratio, using ×32 bump modules. ATPlace2.5D achieves 142.42m total wirelength and 92.3°C maximum temperature compared to TAP-2.5D baseline of 185.20m and 94.1°C.
scenario.architecture: 2.5D-IC with passive interposer on organic substrate, 8 chiplets (CPU, GPU, HBM, DRAM), ×32 D2D interface modules with 32 lanes and 25μm bump pitch, RDL layer with microbumps and epoxy underfill, C4 pillars to substrate, TSVs through interposer, air-forced heatsink with 0.1K/W convective resistance.
scenario.workload: Steady-state worst-case power distribution with power densities ranging from 2×10^5 to 3×10^6 W/m² across chiplets; ambient temperature 45°C.
scenario.operating_point: Maximum temperature (Tmax) = 92.3°C; total wirelength (TWL) = 142.42m; placement runtime 6 minutes; 64×64 HotSpot thermal grid resolution.

original_setup.optimizer: Conjugate Gradient Descent (CGD) with projection function for discrete orientations
original_setup.controller: Multi-objective balancing via λ_therm and λ_dens parameters; Polak-Ribière conjugate direction method
original_setup.benchmark: Case 3 from ATPlace2.5D benchmark: 8 chiplets (CPU, GPU, HBM, DRAM heterogeneous mix), 8448 nets, ×32 D2D interface modules

thermal_observable.location: Maximum temperature (Tmax) across all chiplets on interposer
thermal_observable.aggregation: Peak value over 64×64 HotSpot thermal grid during steady-state worst-case power distribution

physical_mismatches.reason: Quasi-homogeneous approximation (Eq. 6) ignores heterogeneous material interfaces between silicon chiplets, epoxy underfill, microbump arrays, and RDL layer; error concentrates at chiplet edges and interposer boundaries
Infinite space Green's function approximation for compact thermal model assumes chiplets in infinite medium; finite interposer boundaries modeled via mirror method at computational cost
Chiplet thickness in z-direction approximated as t_i·exp(-u²a²) rather than exact integration; fitting parameter 'a' ranges 0 to t_i
2D placement on passive interposer does not capture 3D heat spreading through substrate, C4 pillars, or PCB secondary path; only primary cooling path (TIM-spreader-heatsink) considered
Steady-state thermal analysis assumes worst-case constant power distribution; transient thermal effects during workload transitions not modeled
Orientation limited to discrete {0°, 90°, 180°, 270°} via projection function Bz; continuous gradient optimization then projected to legal angles

studio_assumptions: Passive interposer with no active cooling or power delivery circuits embedded in interposer
Air-forced heatsink with fixed convective resistance 0.1 K/W independent of chiplet placement or thermal profile
Homogeneous epoxy underfill between microbumps with effective thermal conductivity treating microbump arrays as composite material
Adiabatic (zero heat flux) boundary conditions on all lateral surfaces; heat dissipation only through primary TIM-spreader-heatsink path
Microbumps modeled as homogeneous layer; individual bump thermal resistance not discretized
Signal nets only considered (Tx/Rx D2D connections); power and ground distribution addressed in subsequent design stages
Chiplet power as uniform volumetric density within chiplet bounds; no internal power heterogeneity or subcircuit-level thermal gradients
HotSpot 6.0 with 64×64 grid resolution as ground truth for model training and validation
5-10 random legalized placement layouts sufficient for compact model dataset generation and parameter fitting
missing_inputs: No code repository, supplementary data, or detailed model parameters (l_x,i, l_y,i, A, a, B fitting values) disclosed for reproducibility
Hyperparameter optimization via Bayesian (Optuna) method not fully detailed; specific lr_pos, lr_ang, λ_dens,0, λ_therm,0 values for Case 3 not provided
Exact chiplet dimensions (length, width, height, thickness) for Case 3 not enumerated; only stated as heterogeneous CPU/GPU/HBM/DRAM mix with power densities 2×10⁵ to 3×10⁶ W/m²
Chiplet microbump map and D2D interface pin assignments not provided; bump pitch 25μm and ×32 module geometry inferred from Table 4 and Figure 2
Power per chiplet and power map distribution for Case 3 worst-case workload not disclosed
Material properties (thermal conductivity κ, density, specific heat) for silicon, epoxy, RDL, TIM, spreader, heatsink not listed; inherited from references [6, 36] without reproduction
Thermal interface material (TIM) thickness and conductivity not specified; only convective resistance 0.1 K/W given
Heat spreader and heatsink dimensions stated as 2× interposer size (78mm × 78mm) but material properties not provided
Legalization MILP solver details and constraint parameters (ε, w_gap = 100μm) provided but numerical solver tolerances and convergence criteria not documented
No transient or dynamic thermal analysis; steady-state assumption applicability to actual workloads not validated
